answer: To deter Sybil attacks in an agent swarm tracking raven trajectories across a cedar valley, nodes authenticate peers via mutual radio time-difference-of-arrival localization. Agents cross-verify nanosecond timestamps against peer baselines across the local horizon, forcing an adversary to deploy discrete transceivers at unique spatial coordinates per identity. However, multipath reflections from dense foliage cause timing jitter, triggering false authentication drops.
